elements.element: Vendor defends Customer against third-party claims
elements.evidence: "Vendor shall defend and indemnify Customer and its Affiliates against any third-party claim"

elements.element: Trigger: allegation that Services or Deliverables infringe IP
elements.evidence: "(a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right"

elements.element: Trigger: data breach caused by Vendor
elements.evidence: "(c) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor"
"(d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct"
"allow the indemnifying party to control the defence"

elements.element: Customer indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law
elements.evidence: "arising out of content or materials provided by Customer for use in the Services or Customer's breach of Applicable Law"
"an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right"
"Customer's unauthorized modification ... combination with items not supplied by Vendor, or Vendor's compliance with written specifications supplied by Customer"
"Vendor shall procure the right ... modify or replace them ... Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees"

elements.element: Vendor indemnity subject to super-cap of 3× annual fees
elements.evidence: No super-cap language; Section 21.3 only lists indemnification as an Excluded Claim, with no 3× annual fees cap inserted.

offending_extra_words: Vendor's obligation in Section 20.1(a) does not apply to the extent a claim arises from Customer's unauthorized modification of the Services or Deliverables, their combination with items not supplied by Vendor, or Vendor's compliance with written specifications supplied by Customer.
reasons: All preferred atomic elements are present: defend and indemnify Customer and Affiliates; the four triggers (IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data incident, gross negligence/wilful misconduct); notice, control and cooperation only; and a Customer indemnity confined to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
The fallback bargain is incomplete because no 3× annual fees super-cap on Vendor's indemnity was inserted, but that is immaterial since the locked preferred level is satisfied in full.

Minimality fails on the inserted Section 20.2 exclusions: 'usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications)' is a fallback-level element and operates as a new carve-back on the preferred indemnity we just secured, so it changes more than needed to complete the preferred level.

Section 20.5 remedies are justified rather than extra, because existing Section 9.3 already cross-references 'the remedies required by Section 20.5' and omitting them would leave a dangling cross-reference.

Intent is preserved: Sections 9.3, 19.5 and 21.3 remain untouched and effective, and all defined terms used (Affiliates, Services, Deliverables, Customer Data, Applicable Law, Fees) are resolved in the Agreement.
